page: UpCloud GPU-8xCPU-64GB-1xL4 is a KVM-virtualized server featuring an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with x86_64 architecture. The CPU configuration provides 8 vCPUs and 8 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz with a shared allocation model. Cache specifications include 64 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, translating to 8.0 GB per core. Acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, which includes 24 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage and comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities alongside moderate multi-core throughput. The server achieves top-tier status in stress-ng single-core CPU performance, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core stress-ng performance, bzip3 decompression, and PassMark CPU scores fall into the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests also show average performance, with read-only large block speeds at 123.85 GB/sec and write speeds at 66.29 GB/sec. For AI workloads, the NVIDIA L4 GPU delivers top-tier text generation speeds of 402.56 tokens/sec for a small 135M LLM model, though prompt processing for the same model remains in the average tier. A key architectural tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation and the complete absence of local storage, requiring external storage solutions.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a dense allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per core alongside dedicated GPU acceleration, making it a resource-dense option for specialized workloads without the overhead of high-core-count instances. The hardware profile is optimized for workloads such as low-latency LLM inference, machine learning model deployment, single-threaded data compression tasks, and GPU-accelerated compute jobs. It is also suitable for memory-intensive applications that require moderate parallel processing and GPU acceleration but do not demand local NVMe storage.
